h1: Order of Nondisclosure (Record Sealing) Lawyer El Paso, TX
intro: When a case ended in deferred adjudication or a conviction, expunction is usually off the table — but an order of nondisclosure may still seal it from employers, landlords and background-check companies. Attorney Robert Navar files these petitions in the El Paso court that handled your case.
summaryHeading: When expunction is off the table, sealing may still be open
summary: An order of nondisclosure under Texas Government Code Chapter 411, Subchapter E-1 seals a criminal record from the public and from private background-check companies, so most private employers and landlords do not see it.
It does not hide the record from law enforcement, prosecutors, courts, or a list of state licensing and child-care agencies.
Common paths: completed deferred adjudication, certain first misdemeanor convictions, and a qualifying first DWI. Waiting periods vary by section and some offenses are excluded.
We confirm eligibility against the current statute, then quote a flat fee after a free consultation. Not sure whether you need this or an expunction? Call 915-503-1600.

sections.heading: Who Can Still See a Sealed Record
paragraphs: A nondisclosure order tells the court clerk, DPS and the arresting agencies that they may not release the record to the public, and DPS notifies the private background-check vendors that buy its data. The practical effect: when a private employer, apartment complex or volunteer organization runs a check, the case generally does not appear, and in most private settings you may deny its existence on applications — except to the entities that still have access.

Those exceptions matter. Criminal justice agencies keep full access, and a sealed case can still be used for enhancement if you are charged again. The statute also lists state entities that still see it: licensing boards for nurses, teachers, lawyers, peace officers and security guards, school districts, the Department of Family and Protective Services, and others. If you are applying to one of those, you generally must still disclose the case. For federal jobs, military enlistment and security clearances, treat the record as visible and ask us about the specific form.
This is why we check whether an expunction is possible first. Expunction destroys the record outright; nondisclosure is the remedy for cases that cannot be expunged.

sections.heading: The Main Routes to Nondisclosure Under Subchapter E-1
paragraphs: Subchapter E-1 is not one rule but a set of sections, each covering a different way a case can end. Which section applies decides whether you file a petition at all, how long you wait, and what you must prove. Eligibility also depends on your entire criminal history — in general, a later conviction or deferred adjudication for anything other than a fine-only traffic offense can disqualify you.

list.text: for many first-time, non-violent misdemeanors, the statute directs the court to issue the order when it discharges and dismisses the case, after a fee is paid — no separate petition.

for deferred adjudication cases that do not qualify for the automatic order. Many misdemeanors are eligible at discharge or after a waiting period for certain offense categories; felonies carry a longer wait.
a first misdemeanor conviction with probation or a short jail term may be sealed after the waiting period the statute assigns to that sentence.

a qualifying first driving-while-intoxicated conviction may be sealed after a waiting period — shorter where an ignition interlock was used — unless the statute's exclusions apply, such as a crash involving another person or a high alcohol concentration.
cases with a family-violence finding, offenses requiring sex-offender registration, murder, human trafficking, stalking, injury to a child or elderly person and similar offenses are not eligible.

sections.heading: Counting the Waiting Period Correctly
paragraphs: Waiting periods run from the date you were discharged from deferred adjudication or completed your sentence, not from the arrest date. In general a Class C deferred that ended in dismissal is handled by expunction rather than nondisclosure; misdemeanor deferred adjudication is eligible at discharge or after a waiting period for offenses in certain Penal Code chapters; eligible misdemeanor convictions wait the period the statute assigns to that sentence. During the waiting period you must not be convicted of or placed on deferred adjudication for a new offense other than a fine-only traffic ticket.

Those "other than a traffic ticket" words are where many El Paso petitions fail. Fine-only traffic offenses are carved out, but a Class B driving while license invalid or a paid non-traffic Class C like public intoxication may not be. We pull your DPS record and each El Paso court's disposition, and we confirm eligibility against the current statute before filing — the Legislature amends this subchapter regularly.

sections.heading: Which El Paso Court Hears the Petition
paragraphs: Unlike an expunction, which goes to district court, a nondisclosure petition is filed in the court that handled the original case: one of the El Paso County Courts at Law or Criminal Courts at Law for a misdemeanor, or a district court for a felony deferred adjudication. The county and district courts sit at the courthouse at 500 E. San Antonio Ave downtown.

We draft the petition, attach the judgment and discharge order, pay the filing fee, and give the prosecutor notice. The State may request a hearing, and the judge must find that sealing the record is in the best interest of justice. For a client who completed probation cleanly, that finding is often routine; where something needs context — a failure-to-appear warrant that was later recalled, for example — we address it in the petition. Once signed, the clerk sends the order to DPS, which notifies the agencies and private vendors; commercial databases can take time to update.

sections.heading: Private Employer vs. Government Employer After the Order
paragraphs: A private employer in El Paso running a standard pre-employment check should see nothing for the sealed case, and under state law you may generally deny the arrest and prosecution on that application. Apartment screenings, most volunteer checks and private trucking and warehouse employers along I-10 fall in the same category.

Government and licensed employers are different. If you are applying to Fort Bliss as a civilian, to a federal agency, to a hospital, to a school district, or for any state license, assume the agency can see the sealed record and answer accordingly — a sealed case disclosed honestly is far less damaging than one discovered after a denial.

Our fee is a flat amount quoted after a free consultation, with court costs set by the court and disclosed separately. Our record clearing overview compares the two remedies side by side. This page is general information, not legal advice about your case.

faqs.q: Does an order of nondisclosure erase my record?
faqs.a: No. It seals the record from the public and private background-check companies, but law enforcement, courts, prosecutors and a list of state licensing and child-care agencies keep access. Expunction is the remedy that destroys records, and it is available only for certain outcomes such as dismissals and completed Class C deferrals.

faqs.q: I completed deferred adjudication in El Paso. Do I automatically get nondisclosure?
faqs.a: Possibly. For many first-time, non-violent misdemeanor deferred adjudications, the statute directs the court to issue the order at discharge once a fee is paid. If the court did not do so, or your case does not fit that section, we file a petition under the section that does apply. We check the court file to see which it is.

faqs.q: How long do I have to wait to seal a misdemeanor conviction?
faqs.a: It depends on the section. Eligible misdemeanor deferred adjudications are generally available at discharge or after a waiting period for certain offense categories; eligible misdemeanor convictions and a first DWI have their own waiting periods that depend on the sentence and, for DWI, on interlock use. We confirm the current period before filing.

faqs.q: What offenses can never be sealed?
faqs.a: In general, cases with an affirmative family-violence finding, offenses requiring sex-offender registration, murder, capital murder, aggravated kidnapping, human trafficking, stalking, injury to a child or elderly person, and violations of protective orders are excluded. The DWI sections have their own exclusions.

faqs.q: Which court do I file in?
faqs.a: The court that handled the original case — a County Court at Law or Criminal Court at Law for a misdemeanor, or a district court for a felony deferred adjudication. For El Paso County cases that means the courthouse at 500 E. San Antonio Ave downtown.

faqs.q: Can I just handle this myself with the state's form?
faqs.a: Texas publishes a petition form, and some people file it successfully. The problems arise with eligibility: the wrong section, a miscounted waiting period or an overlooked later conviction gets the petition denied and the filing fee spent. A free consultation tells you which kind of case yours is.
